message:
v0.35: Sign in with Apple in the iPhone app, optional, with account deletion

The account panel's Sign in / Sign out / Delete account rows are real now, in the
iOS app only. Everything else about the game is unchanged, and nothing anywhere is
gated on having an account.

Client (index.html, new section ACCOUNT SIGN-IN):
  * Sign in with Apple through a small local Capacitor plugin. The server mints a
    single use nonce (GET /account/nonce), that exact string is handed to Apple,
    Apple echoes it inside the signed identity token, and the server requires the
    two to match. Nothing is hashed on the client: hashing is what you do when the
    party checking the nonce did not mint it, and ours did.
  * The first sign in binds the name this phone is ALREADY playing under, so nobody
    retypes a name they picked months ago. The server's first name set is free, so
    that is safe to attempt automatically; if the name is taken or blocked the
    inline editor opens pre filled with the server's own sentence on it.
  * Signed in, the panel header says "Signed in with Apple" and the note names you.
  * Sign out drops the session on the phone first and tells the server second, so a
    flaky connection can never leave somebody stuck signed in.
  * Delete account asks first, inside the panel, never as a second full screen page,
    with a tick box for also removing your name from the family board. Afterwards it
    explains the Settings, your name, Sign in with Apple step that no app can do for
    you.
  * On the website the same three rows stay in the same place and stay disabled
    behind a plain sentence. No dead Apple button. The web flow needs a domain
    verification Apple would not hand over yet and stays parked.
  * No email is requested from Apple, so none is ever sent or stored.

iOS (app/ios/App/App):
  * AppleSignInPlugin.swift, about 90 lines, ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider, no pod.
  * ViewController.swift registers it via capacitorDidLoad, the supported hook in
    Capacitor 6 and later, because cap sync rewrites the generated plugin list.
  * Main.storyboard points at that view controller.
  * App.entitlements gains com.apple.developer.applesignin.
  * The "Nasty App Store" provisioning profile was regenerated (it had gone INVALID
    the moment the capability was added to the App ID) and now carries all three
    entitlements.

Privacy (privacy.html, support.html): both said the app has no accounts, which is
now false. Rewritten in plain language: what is kept (an Apple sign in identifier,
your chosen game name, your game statistics), what is not (no email, no password
ever, no tracking, no ads, nothing shared), that accounts are optional, and how to
delete one, with a #delete anchor the app links to.

Server: no code change on either server, so no deploy and no parity risk. Sign in
was switched on purely by configuration on Deno Deploy: NASTY_ACCOUNTS_ENABLED=1,
NASTY_APPLE_AUDIENCES=com.pangman.nasty, plus NASTY_CLAIM_WINDOW_OPEN=0 and
NASTY_LEADERBOARD_ACCOUNTS_ONLY=0 set explicitly so the two parked switches cannot
drift open. /leaderboard verified byte identical before and after.

PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 5. Every account call is plain HTTP that an older server
answers with a 404, which the client treats as "not available, stay a guest", and
no websocket message changed.

Tests: new permanent suite server/tests/test_accounts_stage2_signin_2026_07_25.js,
67 checks, driving the real flow end to end against a private server with a local
JWKS and locally minted Apple tokens. Nothing ever contacts Apple. Two assertions
in test_ui_account_panel_2026_07_25.js were updated, not weakened: they used to mean
"accounts do not exist yet" and now mean "a plain browser has no native Sign in with
Apple, so the rows stay put and stay disabled".

Verified in the iOS Simulator: the plugin registers and the panel really does offer
Sign in with Apple.
